lesson.child_mission: Friction is a force between surfaces that opposes sliding. Rougher contact often means more friction; smoother often means less.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same science idea to a new object or material, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Order likely friction high→low for a toy car: carpet; smooth wood; icy-style plastic sheet (if available).

FEEDBACK
Carpet highest; wood middle; smooth plastic lowest (typical).

WATCH FOR
Thinking friction is only “bad” ignores how it helps us walk and hold objects.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Test a block or shoe sole on three surfaces. Measure slide distance with the same gentle push (or ramp). Table results and conclude which surface had most friction.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.
